_about: What Knos can do and how far each thing has got. `stage` is the highest of `stages` that has evidence; scripts/capabilities.py checks the evidence (offline, and against devnet with --rpc) and renders the table in README.md. An exercised signature that no document of this repository gives is left out and filled by the release; nothing is `reproduced` until a document links someone else's run. Only a public program id is evidence for `deployed` and `exercised`: the `knos_*` addresses of programs-v2/program_ids.json and upgrade_gate's own `declare_id!`, each listed under `programs` with the version devnet runs there (`on_chain`). A deployment of a build at an address of its own (the 0.3.14 rehearsal's staging programs) is never evidence: what ran there is said in the capability's note, with its transaction, and the capability stays `tested` until a transaction at a public id exercises it. docs/CAPABILITIES.md lists the rehearsal's transactions.

capabilities.what: Agreed, approved lines become a payment instruction file for the payer's own bank, and the bank's answer marks them paid or payable again.
capabilities.note: `knos statement pay --rail bank` (ISO 20022 pain.001.001.09) and `knos statement status`; the site writes the same bytes (web/rails.js). The file's structure is checked here against the message's own rules; no bank has taken a file, and no money has moved by it.

capabilities.what: A statement exports every line with its purchase order and its two-way or three-way match, and as a cXML invoice.
capabilities.note: `knos statement export --format match|ariba`. File exports, not integrations: no file has been loaded into any procurement or accounting system, and the cXML is best effort, unverified against a live network.

capabilities.what: An agent lists the funded test tasks, takes one, opens the pull request and is paid on the merge, by command or by three read-only MCP tools.
capabilities.note: `knos task list|show|take|submit|why`. Test USDC with no monetary value. Tested against a stand-in forge and the simulator; the tasks open on the public board are funded by Knos.

capabilities.what: A merged pull request that was not paid gets one sentence saying why, and the fix.
capabilities.note: `knos task why`. It names an order funded through a staging copy of the workflows, which never pays at the public ids; the board itself now funds only through the public pinned workflows (tests/test_task_board.py).

capabilities.what: Ten tasks that are not code puzzles each state the evidence that completes them and the outside count they would move.
capabilities.note: tasks/outside/: reproduce, shadow count, fund from the faucet, install, host a judge, compose (read the verifier through the published crate), gate (adopt the upgrade gate), keyholder (an offer, never a holder until seated), tamper (the cheat bounty) and witness (the independently witnessed transaction). Only an account that is not Knos's is counted (scripts/outsiders.py `task_counts`). Completed by an outside account: 0 of each.

capabilities.what: A table generated from the code says, for every route that can move money and every restriction, whether a program, the pinned workflow or nothing enforces it.
capabilities.note: `knos controls matrix`, docs/ENFORCEMENT.md and the site's #enforcement page. Each enforced cell names a test that tries to get round it. Workflow-enforced means the pinned workflow refuses: a repository that runs another workflow is stopped only by what the program enforces, and the table says which cells those are.

capabilities.what: One archive of the evidence carries a verifier of one standard-library file that checks it with no Knos and no network.
capabilities.note: `knos archive make|verify`. It checks RS256 and ES256 signatures against the archived keys, the log's chain, every root and every total. One run on this repository's samples is recorded (docs/archive_verify.json): they carry no signed token, and the verifier says so. One archive of a real period is recorded there too (`real`): month 202610 of one pair, whose three batches are anchored at the public knos_meter on devnet, with the six tokens GitHub signed for them; its verifier, run with no Knos, says 13 checks hold and 5 notes (the log of events starts at number 1; both acknowledgements of the month are signed by keys the founder holds). That pair is the founder's own account on both sides, and no outside party holds an archive.

capabilities.what: A number a sender gave that never arrived is named, and a month is not closed over it unless a correction a party acknowledged explains it.
capabilities.note: `knos events gaps` and `knos events close`; `knos meter close --events LOG` refuses the same way (tests/test_recall_wired.py). One deliverable id is counted once across periods. Tested with test keys; no outside sender numbers anything yet.

capabilities.what: Two holders compare their archives by one root with every difference named, and a retention policy reports what is due without deleting what an open month or dispute needs.
capabilities.note: `knos archive compare` and `knos archive policy`. The policy reports and deletes nothing. No second holder exists outside the tests.

capabilities.what: Every receipt reads in five parts, each one line: identity, execution, acceptance, consequence, assurance; a valid signature on a weak test reads as weak.
capabilities.note: `knos receipt explain`, and the verifier and approver pages read the same view. It is a reading of receipt versions 3 to 5 and adds no field and no version. The earlier row `receipt_five_parts` is what version 3 keeps apart; this is how any receipt is read.

capabilities.what: A supplier is told before working whether four protections hold: fixed criteria, an acceptance deadline, an appeal, predictable payment; and by what each is enforced.
capabilities.note: `knos preflight`, with --strict exiting non-zero when one is lacked. Each row says program, workflow or advice; what is not checked is said, not claimed. No supplier outside this repository has run it.

capabilities.what: A support resolution is an outcome: a ticket counts when it stayed resolved through a window the terms fix, and each accepted one is billed once.
capabilities.note: examples/outcomes/support-resolution with made-up tickets, and a workflow (outcome-support.yml) that signs the count in a job that runs nothing from the repository. Never run on GitHub or on devnet; no support system is connected.

capabilities.what: A netted period is bound to a reserve the buyer locked before the work, spends no more than it holds, and returns what no draw took after the deadline.
capabilities.note: `knos net reserve`; a period with no reserve says it is unsecured and prints the supplier's exposure. The reserve is a standing order of knos_pay as it is: no program change. The round `net-reserve` runs on the simulator (tests/test_round_net_reserve.py); not run at the public ids.

capabilities.what: A financier quotes and buys a closed, reserved period once: the draws then pay the financier, and an unsigned draw is the financier's loss.
capabilities.note: `knos advance quote`, through the program's existing Assign. Knos lends nothing and charges nothing. Tested in the simulator; no financier exists and none has been asked.

capabilities.what: The relay chain asks GitHub again when a start fails, and a watchdog starts a chain only when none is queued or running.
capabilities.note: worker.yml. The 0.3.19 chain ended on one HTTP 500. Tested against a stand-in for the API; the new chain has not run on GitHub yet.

capabilities.what: Relays with their own fee payers fund side by side and through one shared account, and the page keeps what was measured apart from what is derived.
capabilities.note: `python scripts/load.py measure`. Measured once on devnet on 7 October 2026 (4 relays, 40 orders each way, funded by a wallet in a mint made for the run, at the public knos_pay): 0.46 confirmed transactions a second apart and 0.52 through one shared account, 0 retries, 0 failures; docs/LOAD.md prints it apart from the derived bound. One run through one public endpoint, each relay waiting for a confirmation before it sends again: a reading of that day, not a capacity.

capabilities.what: The first screen's round follows one transaction through seven beats: agree, fails, passes, statement, replay, pay, verify.
capabilities.note: A replay of recorded data (web/demo_data.json). The two statements and the export are computed in the reader's browser from the site's sample; the last beat also shows one recorded run of the stand-alone verifier. The story page and the demonstration's script tell the same seven.

capabilities.what: A page is added to the site by one line, and a build that lacks its module or its data does not offer it.
capabilities.note: Approve, Pay by bank, Enforcement and For judges are added this way. Each is fetched on first opening.

capabilities.what: A checker reads the documents and the site against the capability list, the source and the price book, and fails on a contradiction.
capabilities.note: `python scripts/truth_check.py`, run by CI and the release. It finds six kinds of contradiction, each with a planted case in its tests. It reads sentences by pattern: a contradiction worded another way passes.

capabilities.what: Every description of Knos that a registry, a plugin list or the site serves is the one sentence, and a check fails on any other.
capabilities.note: `python scripts/public_face.py --check` reads this tree; `--remote` reads what PyPI, the MCP registry and GitHub serve and prints the command that corrects each. Until 0.3.20 is published those places still serve older words; glama.json has no description field.

capabilities.what: The billing rule prints three places where the price does not cover the cost, each with its number and its design, and labels every margin gross.
capabilities.note: docs/UNIT_COSTS.md. The costs are budgets and local measurements, not a customer's: nothing has been sold.

capabilities.what: Acceptance is charged once whichever rail pays, and a rail's own charge is shown apart from the software price.
capabilities.note: `knos bill` and src/knos/billing.py (tests/test_billing.py::test_rail_charges_are_shown_apart_from_the_software_price). No invoice has been issued: there is no legal entity to invoice from.

capabilities.what: Each link of the network loop has one counter, read from job records or kept by hand, and none counts events.
capabilities.note: docs/MARKET.md section 7, and `devnet.stats.loop` of the published statistics. All six read 0 today: with no outside buyer the three chain counters are 0 by arithmetic.

capabilities.what: A comment `/knos reserve <amount> for @supplier until <date>` locks a reserve for one supplier through the pinned funding workflow and says its id, amount, deadline and how the supplier checks it.
capabilities.note: Runs on the workflow's fakes and, in the round `net-reserve`, on the simulator. Not run at the public ids: the pinned workflows are republished at 0.3.21 by the release run.

capabilities.what: An organisation's money in a Squads v4 vault: the approval policy becomes the vault's members, threshold, time lock and a separate config authority, and an approval funds only the one commitment it names.
capabilities.note: `knos boundary plan`. Squads v4 is Squads Labs' deployed program, not Knos's; the tests that run it in LiteSVM need its bytes fetched from devnet (scripts/squads_program.py) and skip without them. No vault has been set up by a buyer; nobody outside uses it.

capabilities.what: `knos exit --before-upgrade` lists every order and Balance of an owner, the instruction that takes its money out and whether that lands before a pending upgrade can execute.
capabilities.note: On the simulator with a pending proposal. Held and warranty money cannot leave before an upgrade, and the command says so (docs/GOVERNANCE.md).

capabilities.what: `python scripts/provenance.py verify-proposal N` compares one upgrade proposal's buffer with the verified build's hash and, if asked, with a build of your own.
capabilities.note: Reads the chain and the verified-build record; the tests use fixed accounts. Not yet run against a live proposal by anyone outside.

capabilities.what: A drill where GitHub rotates its signing key mid-period: what verification does with the new key id, what breaks if nobody admits it, and how long recovery takes.
capabilities.note: On the test builds with the tests' fakes (docs/DRILLS.md). Not drilled at the public ids.

capabilities.what: On the judge's host a submission meets limits: a fork bomb stops at the process limit, a write outside its work folder is refused, CPU, memory, file size and time are capped, and the time limit kills the whole tree.
capabilities.note: Linux. What macOS and Windows runners can and cannot enforce is in docs/ATTESTOR.md. The hermetic container is the default where the runner has one; the host sandbox is the fallback and the verdict says so.

capabilities.what: A month closes only when both parties signed its last line, or one did and closed it after the silence the terms allow; an event missing or changed after an acknowledgement is a named discrepancy.
capabilities.note: Ed25519 acknowledgements; the archive carries them and the stand-alone verifier checks them. No outside party has signed one.

capabilities.what: Every export row, the paid record answer and every statement line carry a receipt's five parts (identity, execution, acceptance, consequence, assurance), and terms can require a minimum assurance level for payment.
capabilities.note: A parts file beside each export names it by its sha256; one that leaves a row or a part out is refused. The funding workflow refuses a payment under terms whose `checks.min_assurance` its evaluator cannot reach.

capabilities.what: The watchdog counts a relay run alive only by the heartbeat it writes after its install, cancels and replaces a run stuck in its install wait, and two watchdogs never start two chains.
capabilities.note: Tested with fake runs. It also runs when a worker run ends and from the release step; not yet observed on GitHub's timer at the public ids.

capabilities.what: An event (a comment, a merge) is recorded in the relay log by the event's own run before anything reads it, so the chain's polling is a backstop.
capabilities.note: Tested locally; not yet run on the public worker.

capabilities.what: Workers are partitioned by order: an order's tokens go to one worker, and two workers never take the same order.
capabilities.note: Tested locally; not yet run on the public worker.

capabilities.what: `python scripts/load.py measure --pay` measures end-to-end PayOrder capacity with N relays, each with its own fee payer, counting every attempt with its failures.
capabilities.note: The simulator proves the path and counts; it gives no rate. End-to-end PayOrder capacity on devnet has not been measured: the release run measures it.

capabilities.what: Approving on the approver's screen writes an approval record (policy and version, who, when, why, the evidence's hashes) that the page checks again later: it still matches its evidence, or it was changed.

tested.names: an approval record names the policy and its version

capabilities.note: In the browser, with no account and nothing kept. Ordinary lines resolve in one action; exceptions are read. No buyer has used it.

capabilities.what: A supplier's finance lead sees what is funded with its transaction, the acceptance window and its countdown, appeal rights and the predictable payment date, read from the order's account with no wallet.
capabilities.note: Reads devnet with one call. No supplier's finance lead has used it.

capabilities.what: A page for each vendor the Agent PR Index rates: its numbers with their sample, a right of reply printed word for word, its disputes and their outcome, and how to earn the supplier badge.
capabilities.note: Replies received: 0. Disputes opened by a vendor: 0.

capabilities.what: An independently witnessed transaction a stranger with only a GitHub account runs end to end: terms and a budget, failing then passing work, both statements, a replay refused, the payment, and the stand-alone verifier on the archive.
capabilities.note: Simulated sequence. Completed by an outside account: 0 (task kind `witness`).

capabilities.what: `knos recall approval COMMITMENT` answers from the buyer's memory alone, after a restart, who approved what under which policy version and whether its evidence still matches.
capabilities.note: In the Sibyl memory engine (one entity per commitment, one journal event per decision). `knos recall supplier` answers what a supplier brings from other buyers, only what was granted.

capabilities.what: `knos bill margin --sensitivity` prints, for the worked customers, revenue and gross margin at a realised Acceptance rate of 30, 20, 10 and 5 basis points, credits and rebates applied.
capabilities.note: Worked customers, not sales: nothing has been sold, and on devnet every fee is test money and zero revenue.

capabilities.what: The relay pays each order's fee into one of K token accounts of Knos's fee owner, chosen by the order, and shares pay work out by order, with no program change.
capabilities.note: knos_pay takes any token account the fee owner holds for the mint; `knos relay fee-accounts --k N` plans the accounts and `--execute` makes them. Tested in the simulator against the compiled programs. On devnet six seeded fee accounts exist since 8 Oct 2026 (K = 4 for devnet USDC and the faucet's test USDC, owned by the fee owner, made by the project's own relayer key; docs/RELAY.md lists them); the public worker runs with K = 1, so no payment has used them, and the one-relay rate measured on 8 Oct (0.097 a second) is the only measured rate.

capabilities.what: Recalled history changes what Knos recommends: preflight names the protection a remembered ending calls for, and the approver's queue ranks and labels repeated endings.
capabilities.note: With no memory, neither does (both tests check it); also tests/test_recall.py, test_the_queue_is_ranked_and_labelled_from_memory_and_without_it_nothing_is. Recalled from the memory engine on this machine; nothing is shared between buyers.

capabilities.what: Knos's fee account only receives fees and may lower a rate: no program line lets it sign a verdict, pick a payee or move an order, the modules that make verdicts know no fee, and the fee reads the amount and the rate only.
capabilities.note: A check of the source, not an outside review: it shows what the code allows, and docs/DISPUTES.md says how verdicts and appeals stay with the parties' judges and arbiters.
